10 units, each with key ideas, worked examples, a 10-mark exam-style question, common mistakes and quick recall

How this book matches your exam. Paper 1 is source-based and set on one prescribed subject:

  1. military leaders;
  2. conquest and its impact;
  3. the move to global war;
  4. rights and protest;
  5. conflict and intervention.

For exams up to and including 2027 (the current guide):

  • 1 hour; 24 marks; 30% (SL) and 20% (HL); four sources plus a visual source;
  • four questions:
QuestionTaskMarks
1(a)Comprehension of a source3
1(b)The message of a visual source2
2Value and limitations (origin, purpose, content)4
3Compare and contrast two sources6
4Sources + own knowledge essay9

> From May 2028 (new guide): Paper 1 becomes 1 hour 15 minutes, built around an inquiry question; the OPCVL-style question is removed; outside knowledge is not formally assessed. The source skills in this book still apply.

Examples use the move to global war (Japanese, German and Italian expansion). The practice sources are written for StudyStarx, and are not real documents. The mark allocations are our own guides, written in the style of IB markschemes.

Unit 1 of 10: How Paper 1 Works

Key ideas

  • A source booklet with 4–5 sources (text and visual) on one case study of your prescribed subject.
  • You have 5 minutes of reading time before writing.
  • The questions rise in demand, from comprehension (Q1) to evaluation (Q2), comparison (Q3) and synthesis (Q4).
  • Timing: about 2.5 minutes per mark (Q4 needs about 20–25 minutes).

Worked examples

Example 1: a timing plan: Q1, 7 minutes; Q2, 10 minutes; Q3, 15 minutes; Q4, 25 minutes; 3 minutes to check.

Example 2: reading time: identify each source's origin, then skim the questions.

Example 3: in Q4, use all the sources and your own knowledge.

10-mark exam-style question

(a) List the four Paper 1 questions with their marks. [4]

(b) Create a timing plan for Paper 1. [3]

(c) Explain why Q4 needs the most time. [3]

Answers:

  • (a) Q1(a) 3, Q1(b) 2, Q2 4, Q3 6, Q4 9 (A4).
  • (b) As in Example 1 (A3).
  • (c) It carries the most marks (9) and requires the synthesis of several sources with your own knowledge into a focused argument (R3).

Common mistakes

  1. Spending too long on Q1.
  2. Not using the reading time.
  3. Ignoring the visual source.
  4. Leaving Q4 rushed.
  5. Not knowing the question types in advance.

Quick recall

  1. How many marks is Paper 1?
  2. How long is it?
  3. What is Q2 about?
  4. How many marks is Q4?
  5. What is the SL weighting?

Answers: 1) 24. 2) 1 hour (+5 minutes of reading). 3) Value and limitations. 4) 9. 5) 30%.
